The basic area deals with the question of where AI already plays a role in everyday life. “The first competency is recognizing the role and influence of AI in different contexts,” explains Rampelt. For example, learners could play “AI or not” with their teacher. "Using examples such as smart home devices, social media or apps, they can classify each example based on whether it uses AI or not."

Read more after the ad

Further skills include describing how AI functions and classifying the resource consumption of AI systems. “It’s important that we don’t all constantly use ChatGPT on our cell phones to answer every question,” warns Rampelt. Every time generative AI is used, resources are consumed, which many people are not aware of in everyday life.

Podcast: AI Update

How intelligent is artificial intelligence actually? What consequences does generative AI have for our work, our leisure time and society? In Heise's "AI Update" we, together with The Decoder, bring you updates on the most important AI developments three times a week. On Fridays we examine the different aspects of the AI ​​revolution with experts.

Materials for Germany

Ethical questions run through the entire framework. At the knowledge level, it is about distortions, so-called biases, and their social consequences. At the competency level, critical thinking is linked to ethical aspects, while at the attitude level, a sense of responsibility is considered particularly necessary. According to Rampelt, responsible AI design includes principles such as fairness, transparency and accountability.

The KI Campus is already providing supplementary materials for German-speaking countries. “We believe that for use at the state and regional level, local contextualization is also necessary,” explains Rampelt. Universities and schools are developing their own implementation ideas through an ideas competition with the TÜV SÜD Foundation. “Our goal is to gradually make online courses and educational materials available for the different areas of competence, which can then also be used in class,” says Rampelt.

title: Rinnovabili, in Emilia-Romagna in autorizzazione progetti per 1.146 MW
summary: Sono fermi nella procedura di valutazione ambientale. Grande concentrazione di agrivoltaico nella provincia di Ferrara
full_text:
Nelle campagne di Ferrara il sole c’è, e non manca neppure la terra. Sui crinali dell’Appennino il vento invece arriva solo dove la geografia lo concede, ma i vincoli paesaggistici spesso lo fermano. È qui che si gioca la partita delle rinnovabili in Emilia Romagna: regione industriale, energivora, abituata a correre, ma ancora indietro sull’elettricità verde. Appena il 21% della produzione regionale arriva da fonti rinnovabili, mentre la quota sul totale dei consumi energetici oscilla tra il 15 e il 18%. Il primo numero è 1.146 MW. È la potenza dei progetti di fotovoltaico, agrivoltaico ed eolico oggi in procedure di sola Via (valutazione di impatto ambientale), senza autorizzazione unica regionale: 735 MW riguardano il solare agricolo, altri 411 l’eolico.

Chiedilo al Sole

Domande di approfondimento generate da 24Ore AI

sulla base del contenuto visualizzato.

Il nodo più grosso è Ferrara, dove si concentrano 627 MW di agrivoltaico: investimenti potenziali che raccontano il conflitto con il mondo di chi coltiva la terra. Sul vento la graduatoria cambia: Parma è in testa con 136 megawatt, seguita da Bologna con 107 e Rimini con 72. Numeri piccoli rispetto ai grandi parchi del Sud, ma pesanti dove le aree ventose sono poche e spesso sotto vincolo. Alla coda regionale si aggiunge un secondo pacchetto nazionale: circa un gigawatt di impianti offshore, tra eolico e fotovoltaico galleggiante, con Via statale già approvata ma ancora in attesa dei bandi per gli incentivi del Fer 2: è qui che svetta il progetto Agnes per l’eolico offshore a Ravenna, uno dei più grandi d’Italia. Infine ci sono sette Via statali positive, ma senza autorizzazione unica, per altri 480 MW circa di fotovoltaico.

Vincenzo Colla, vicepresidente della Regione con delega alla green economy, respinge però l’idea di un territorio fermo. «È noto che l’Emilia Romagna non ha l’idroelettrico della Lombardia, del Veneto, della Val d’Aosta e del Piemonte, che permette di fare volumi molto alti», osserva. E sull’eolico aggiunge: «È inutile girarci attorno, c’è un conflitto territoriale tra chi dice tutto bene e chi tutto male. Bisogna cercare il maggior consenso possibile». Il riferimento va anche al progetto Agnes al largo di Ravenna: «Ha già tutti i permessi. Si sta solo aspettando il bando che determini una tariffa idonea a garantire l’investimento».

Nel frattempo, la Regione corre sul cronoprogramma del Pniec. Al 31 maggio 2026 l’Emilia Romagna è all’88,79% del target 2026 sulle rinnovabili elettriche installate: restano 281 MW da realizzare entro fine anno, sui 2.504 complessivi contati dal 2021. Terna indica, nei primi cinque mesi, 223 MW aggiuntivi di fotovoltaico, terza crescita dopo Sicilia e Lombardia.

La svolta, almeno normativa, dovrebbe essere arrivata con la legge regionale sulle aree idonee, che l’Emilia Romagna ha approvato a maggio entro i tempi previsti dalla normativa, e che individua le zone dove accelerare gli impianti, privilegiando aree produttive, coperture, parcheggi e spazi già compromessi. Il testo fissa anche paletti agricoli: limite massimo dell’1,5% della Sau (superficie agricola utilizzata) regionale e del 2% della Sau comunale. «Dopo ritardi che dipendevano anche dalla legislazione nazionale, in regione in due mesi abbiamo fatto la legge», rivendica Colla.

In the countryside of Ferrara the sun is there, and there is no shortage of earth either. On the ridges of the Apennines, however, the wind reaches only where geography allows it, but landscape constraints often stop it. This is where the game of renewables is being played in Emilia Romagna: an industrial, energy-intensive region, used to running, but still behind on green electricity. Just 21% of regional production comes from renewable sources, while the share of total energy consumption fluctuates between 15 and 18%. The first number is 1,146 MW. This is the power of photovoltaic, agrivoltaic and wind projects today in one-way procedures (environmental impact assessment), without single regional authorisation: 735 MW concern agricultural solar, another 411 wind power.

Ask the Sun

The biggest node is Ferrara, where 627 MW of agrivoltaics are concentrated: potential investments that illustrate the conflict with the world of those who cultivate the land. Regarding wind, the ranking changes: Parma is in the lead with 136 megawatts, followed by Bologna with 107 and Rimini with 72. Small numbers compared to the large parks in the South, but heavy where windy areas are few and often under constraints. A second national package is added to the regional queue: approximately one gigawatt of offshore plants, including wind and floating photovoltaic, with a state road already approved but still awaiting tenders for the Fer 2 incentives: this is where the Agnes project for offshore wind in Ravenna stands out, one of the largest in Italy. Finally, there are seven positive state roads, but without single authorization, for approximately another 480 MW of photovoltaic.

Vincenzo Colla, vice president of the Region with responsibility for the green economy, however rejects the idea of ​​a fixed territory. «It is known that Emilia Romagna does not have the hydroelectric power of Lombardy, Veneto, Val d'Aosta and Piedmont, which allows for very high volumes», he observes. And on wind energy he adds: «There is no point in beating around the bush, there is a territorial conflict between those who say everything is good and those who say everything is bad. We need to seek as much consensus as possible." The reference also goes to the Agnes project off the coast of Ravenna: «It already has all the permits. We are just waiting for the tender that determines a suitable tariff to guarantee the investment."

In the meantime, the Region runs on the Pniec timetable. As of 31 May 2026, Emilia Romagna is at 88.79% of the 2026 target for installed renewable electricity: 281 MW remain to be achieved by the end of the year, out of a total of 2,504 counted from 2021. Terna indicates, in the first five months, 223 additional MW of photovoltaic, the third growth after Sicily and Lombardy.

The turning point, at least in terms of legislation, should have come with the regional law on suitable areas, which Emilia Romagna approved in May within the time required by law, and which identifies the areas where the plants can be accelerated, favoring production areas, roofs, car parks and spaces that are already compromised. The text also sets agricultural limits: maximum limit of 1.5% of the regional UAA (used agricultural area) and 2% of the municipal UAA. «After delays that also depended on national legislation, in the region we passed the law in two months», claims Colla.
